title: The Linga Purana
author: vyasa
attributionNote: Ascribed to Vyasa and compiled over several centuries. Its name comes from the linga, the aniconic form of Shiva that its first part explains and glorifies.
description: The Linga Purana teaches the worship of Shiva under the sign of the linga: the greatness of Shiva and of his devotees, the cosmic cycles and the dissolution of the worlds, the incarnations of Shiva and the destruction of Daksha's sacrifice, and then the rules for the linga's installation, the recitation of its thousand names and the observance of Shivaratri.
historicalContext: Composed for the growing Shaiva communities of early medieval India, it belongs with the Shiva, Skanda and Matsya Puranas as the scriptural library of Shiva worship, and its ritual chapters record how the linga came to stand at the centre of a temple.
availabilityNote: Complete: the Sanskrit text of all 108 chapters of the first part as GRETIL publishes it, streamed from GRETIL at read time, one chapter at a time. This is the original Sanskrit, not a translation.
